removability.rationale: Route deletion is trivial and links live in only two places, but the feature leaves traces across the data layer, the shared card type and the card component, so removal is a handful of scattered (if findable, type-checker-guided) edits rather than delete-a-directory.

changeability.rationale: Most rules (sprite URL, naming, dex numbers, missing-value rendering) are single-definition and the shared card render point means one fix covers every list; the duplicated effect-fallback and slot-sorting logic, plus a delicate home-page query state machine, keep it below excellent.

coupling.rationale: Layering is genuinely loose: routes → per-page server functions → one API module, with strict TS at every seam and a real server/client boundary. The tangles are small and local (root-loader shape coupling, a private router field, the team page's dual state).

abstraction_design.rationale: The two abstractions that matter (card lists, reference→card conversion) are designed around the app's actual variation and stretch to new cases without copying; the residual duplication is confined to trivial link lists and a slowly-widening card DTO.

findings.issue: The abilities-only 'hidden' concept is threaded through the shared CardData type and rendered by the generic Pokémon card, so one feature leaks into an abstraction used by all five lists.
findings.suggestion: Give PokemonCardList an optional note/footer render-prop (like the existing renderAction) and let the ability page pass the 'Hidden ability' text, keeping CardData generic.

findings.issue: The 'short_effect, else latest flavor text, else —' fallback rule is duplicated verbatim between getMovePage and getAbilityPage; a spec change to the rule needs two edits.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared effectText(entries, flavorEntries) helper next to latestEnglish/collapse in pokeapi.ts.

findings.issue: The team page mixes server-derived data (members, coverage computed from the cookie at request time) with client team state, filtering by name and calling router.invalidate() on removal — two sources of truth that must be kept in sync by hand.
findings.suggestion: Either compute coverage on the client from the shared type data (types change rarely) or drive the member list from the client team and only use the server fn for coverage, making the reconciliation explicit in one place.

findings.issue: head() checks the private match field m._notFound in addition to the public m.status === 'notFound'.
findings.suggestion: Drop m._notFound and rely on the public status; private fields can disappear without notice.

findings.issue: useMediaBase couples every sprite-rendering component to the root loader's return shape via a string route id; renaming or reshaping the root loader breaks cards at a distance.
findings.suggestion: Pass mediaBase through a small context provider in __root.tsx (like TeamProvider) or make the root loader's type a named exported interface both sides import.

findings.issue: Pokémon-type slot sorting ([...x].sort((a,b)=>a.slot-b.slot)) is repeated three times across two server functions.
findings.suggestion: Add a typesInSlotOrder(pokemon) helper in pokeapi.ts next to the other projection helpers.

findings.issue: getConfig bundles unrelated concerns (env-derived mediaBase and the team cookie), so removing the team feature later means editing the root config path.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for now; if more page-independent config appears, split into dedicated small server functions.

findings.issue: The link=true|false boolean flag is mild flag creep in the one shared badge component.
findings.suggestion: Fine at this size; if a third variant appears (e.g. plain text with a count), switch to a variant prop or two small components.

summary: This is a well-layered TanStack Start app: routes are thin, all API access and caching live behind one server module, and the two load-bearing abstractions (PokemonCardList, toCards) genuinely absorb the app's variation so the five Pokémon-card lists share one implementation and one sprite logic. Editing it is mostly a matter of touching one obvious place, with strict TypeScript catching leftovers. The main debt is small: an abilities-specific field leaking into the shared card type, a duplicated effect-fallback rule, and a team page that reconciles server and client state by hand.

Strict TS makes each leftover a compile error, so nothing dead survives silently — but it's ~6 files, not 2.

The wrinkle is the team page, which must keep insertion order per FEATURE.md, so in practice you add a sort prop and pass it from the four non-team call sites — still one component plus one-line changes.
